Dangling-reference repairs:
- "Let me now say only this, that truth is ONE SPECIES OF GOOD…": referring words "Let me now say only this, that". First-person cut (author's framing only).
- "Pragmatism says no, and I fully agree with her.": referring word "I". Author name span `I{, }William James{, }`, taken from the frontmatter `source:` line. I placed it here rather than cutting "and I fully agree with her". This clause is the author's endorsement of the doctrine, as distinct from the Schiller/Dewey account. It is also the only "I" before the later first-person case ("My belief in the Absolute…", "Grant that it may be true in giving me…"). That case is made of "my"/"me" statements where an author span cannot attach, and naming the author here resolves them. Flagged for review, since a cut was arguably available.
- "I said just now that what is better for us to believe is true UNLESS…": referring words "I said just now that". Cut (pointing only).
- "She has in fact no prejudices whatever…": referring word "She". Name span "Pragmatism" (quoted from "Pragmatism says no" in this segment), joined with `{}`. The earlier antecedent ("her" in the "Pragmatism says no" statement) is far back, and the "it"s about the Absolute come between. Later "she"/"her" then resolve to it.
- In "Nevertheless, as I conceive it,--and let me speak now confidentially…" I kept the whole sentence. "as I conceive it" and "merely in my own private person" limit the claim to the author's own view, so neither was cut. The "I"/"me"/"my" are resolved by the author name span.

"We"/"you" judged generic and left unrepaired: "Surely you must admit this"; "our duty"; "we are fond of"; "help us to lead"; "better for us", "what we OUGHT to believe", "none of you", "Ought we ever not…", "can we then keep…" (author and audience together); "Probably you also agree", "if we practically did believe…", "Your suspicion…", "when you pass from…"; "any particular belief of ours", "our truths"; "But we cannot easily thus restrict our hypotheses"; "what works best in the way of leading us"; "But you see already…".

Dropped statements:
- "To answer this difficulty fully is impossible at this stage of my account." Transition. "this difficulty" points back outside the segment.
- "You touch here upon the very central point of Messrs. Schiller's, Dewey's and my own doctrine of truth, which I cannot discuss with detail until my sixth lecture." Transition and forward hook.
- The food analogy in "just as certain foods are not only agreeable to our taste, but good for our teeth, our stomach and our tissues; so". This is an illustration, cut mid-sentence with joining text `{, }`. The proposition about ideas is kept.
- "You see by this what I meant when I called pragmatism a mediator and reconciler and said, borrowing the word from Papini, that he unstiffens our theories." It points back to earlier claims ("what I meant when I called"). No cut leaves a statement, and its content restates claims made outside the segment.
- "In my last lecture I shall return again to the relations of pragmatism with religion." Forward hook.

No outside-frame references kept. No asides.
